claim.value: An absent report must be distinguished from a recorded zero and cannot be treated as establishing zero work.

provenance.rationale: Both the operational distinction and the prohibition on inferring zero work from an absent report are explicit.

signal_basis.value: The procedure distinguishes missing reports from recorded zeros. Its prospective signal consists of repeated pattern alignment consistent with independent dates and additional histories; a suspected reporting omission gains support when histories explain the exposed inconsistency.
signal_basis.scope: Interpretation of daily records, assuming the described prospective signal occurs.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the missing-versus-zero distinction, corroborated alignment signal, omission check and prospective qualification.
The claim is supported without requiring an unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: An absent report supplies no recorded work quantity. Alignment and corroborating histories may support identifying a reporting omission, but the omission alone does not establish that no work occurred. The claim correctly preserves this evidential distinction.
uncertainty: Actual work on an unreported day remains undetermined by the absence alone; this does not weaken the claimed restriction.
